items.title: Dave Brubeck — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...Cal Lampley. Do you remember that name?

ctx.x: At Columbia – when I think of Columbia during that period, I know one of the influential people there is John Hammond. Hammond was an admirer of your music, but I don’t often hear his name in association with your time at Columbia. Did you have any dealings with John when you were at Columbia?
No, and I kept thinking I would have. But it was different artists represented the guys that – Cal Lampley. Do you remember that name? The first jazz that Teo [Macero]
ever did was, I believe, with me. So, in a way, I broke him into the business. He’s such a sharp guy. He caught on quite quickly.
